recipes.title: Menemen
recipes.summary: Turkey's egg sauce uses green pepper and spring onion instead of tatashe, and the eggs stay soft and wet. Wara stands in for Turkish white cheese and a pinch of ata rodo for the pepper flakes.

Add the tomato and ata rodo. Cook 5 minutes until the tomato collapses into a loose sauce.
Crack the eggs straight into the pan and stir slowly over low heat. Stop while they are still glossy and a little runny.

Rub the hot toast with the cut garlic.
Spoon the tomato pulp over, drizzle with oil and finish with torn scent leaf.

recipes.title: Garlic Mushroom Toast

Toss, add the garlic and cook 2 minutes more.
Take off the heat, stir in the yoghurt, parsley, spring onion and seasoning.
Pile onto hot toast.

recipes.title: Tomato & Egg Stir-Fry
recipes.summary: China's home-cooking staple: eggs scrambled fast, then folded through a quick tomato sauce. No wine or sesame needed; a pinch of sugar and spring onion carry it.

Add the sugar, salt and water. Simmer 2 minutes until saucy.
Return the eggs, fold through for 30 seconds and finish with the green spring onion.
recipes.tip: Ripe, soft tomatoes break down fastest. Firm ones need a splash more water.

Heat half the oil in a small pan, pour in half the mix and swirl thin.

Add the tomato and cook 3 minutes until it softens but still holds shape.

Pour in the beaten eggs and fold slowly until creamy.
Stir in the cheese and scent leaf and serve.

recipes.summary: Iran's tomato omelette is a slow-cooked tomato sauce with turmeric that the eggs are set into. Fresh Basket turmeric grated in, a whole ata rodo for gentle heat, bread or yam alongside.

Add the tomato and the whole ata rodo. Simmer 12 to 15 minutes until jammy.
Beat the eggs, pour over, and stir slowly until just set. Remove the pepper.
Serve with bread.
recipes.tip: Leave the ata rodo whole for aroma without heat; chop it if you want fire.

recipes.summary: The Italian oven omelette done on the hob with a lid, since not every Lagos kitchen has an oven. Broccoli and spring onion from the box; swap in tatashe and spinach, or mushrooms, for other days.
steps: Whisk the eggs, milk, salt, pepper and paprika.
In a lidded non-stick pan, fry the broccoli and spring onion in the oil 4 minutes. Add garlic for 30 seconds.
Pour in the eggs, scatter cheese on top, cover and cook on the lowest heat 15 to 18 minutes until set in the middle.
Slide out, cut into wedges.

recipes.summary: A folded omelette with sliced tomato, garlic and greens. Baby spinach or ugu, wara for feta, a little spring onion.
steps: Fry the garlic and tomato slices in the oil for a minute each side.
Add the spinach and let it wilt, 30 seconds.
Pour in the beaten, seasoned eggs and tilt the pan so they spread.
When the base is set, scatter the cheese and spring onion, fold and serve.

Beat the eggs with the rest of the herbs and the spring onion.
Cook two thin omelettes in the remaining oil, folding each in half.
Plate the omelette, salad, avocado and a spoon of yoghurt together.

Mix the tomato, onion, coriander, chilli, lime juice and salt.

recipes.title: Chunky Vegetable Stew (Ata Dindin Style)
recipes.summary: Instead of blending everything, the tatashe, tomatoes and onion are cut in big pieces and fried hard so the stew has bite and colour. Oil is halved; beef, tripe, iru and crayfish are left to the customer.
steps: Heat the oil until it shimmers. Fry the sliced onion 3 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger for 1 minute, then the tatashe. Fry on high 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until the edges blister.
Add the tomato wedges and ata rodo. Keep the heat high and fry 8 to 10 minutes; the tomatoes should soften but still hold their shape.
Season with thyme, stock powder and salt. Stir in the diced onion and cook 2 minutes more so it stays crunchy.
Serve over rice or yam, or spoon beside your protein.
recipes.tip: Do not cover the pan. Steam turns a fried stew into a boiled one.

recipes.title: Nigerian Mixed Vegetable Sauce

steps: Boil the potato cubes 8 minutes until almost done. Drain.
Fry the onion in the oil 2 minutes. Add carrots and green beans, 4 minutes.
Add tomato chunks, curry, thyme and stock cube with a splash of water. Simmer 5 minutes.
Add potato, cabbage and green pepper. Toss 4 minutes so the cabbage softens but keeps colour.
Finish with spring onion and salt.
recipes.tip: Cut everything the same size so it cooks evenly and looks like the party version.

recipes.summary: A lighter, greens-first efo riro: fresh ugu or efo tete instead of frozen spinach, far less oil, and the pepper base chopped rather than blended so it reads as a vegetable sauce. Smoked fish or beef is the customer's call.

Cook on medium-high 12 minutes until thick and the oil separates.
Season with curry, thyme and the stock cube.
Pile in the greens, stir, cover 2 minutes, then uncover and cook 3 minutes until just wilted and still bright.
Stir in the scent leaf and serve.

recipes.title: Stewed Okra & Tomatoes

steps: Soften the onion in the oil 4 minutes. Add garlic and paprika for 1 minute.
Add tomato, ata rodo and a quarter cup of water. Simmer 5 minutes.
Add okra and lemon juice, cover and simmer 12 minutes until tender.
Season, stir in scent leaf and serve.
recipes.tip: The lemon juice is not just flavour; the acid keeps the okra from going gluey.

steps: Cook the onion slowly in the oil 8 minutes until golden.
Take off the heat, stir in the paprika (it burns easily), then add the peppers and garlic.

Add the tomato wedges and chilli, cover and simmer 20 minutes. Season.

Add all the pepper strips and cook on medium 10 minutes, stirring often.

Add tomato, ata rodo and basil. Simmer 15 minutes until thick.

Scatter parsley and serve.

steps: Char the tatashe over a flame or in a dry pan until blackened, steam in a covered bowl, peel and chop.
Put tomatoes, peppers, garlic, chilli, oil, paprika and salt in a wide pan.
Simmer gently, uncovered, stirring every 15 minutes, for about 2 hours until dark, thick and glossy.
Cool and keep in a jar in the fridge up to a week.
recipes.tip: A wide pan matters more than anything else: more surface means faster evaporation.

Toss with cooked pasta and basil.

steps: Soften onion, green pepper and garlic in the oil 6 minutes.
Add tomato, tomato paste, ata rodo, rosemary and stock. Simmer 25 minutes until reduced by a third.
Stir in butter, spring onion and parsley. Spoon over fish and rice.
recipes.tip: Make it while the fish fries; both finish at the same time.
recipes.serveWith: Fried or grilled fish with white rice. You add: the fish, stock cube, oil, butter.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin K intake: one serving gives about 71% of your daily vitamin K from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Onions supply quercetin and prebiotic fibre that feeds gut bacteria. Green pepper adds vitamin C and fibre with very few calories.

recipes.title: Bhuna Masala (Onion-Tomato Curry Base)
recipes.summary: The Indian 'stew base': a kilo of onions cooked down with tomato, garlic, ginger, fresh turmeric and spices into a paste you freeze in portions. Groundnuts replace cashews. A spoonful with green beans, cauliflower or boiled eggs is dinner.
steps: Blend garlic, ginger, chillies and groundnuts to a paste.
Fry cumin seeds in the oil, add onions and cook 25 minutes, stirring, until deep golden.
Add the paste and turmeric, 5 minutes. Add tomato puree and ground spices.
Cook on low 45 to 60 minutes, stirring, until the oil separates and the paste is dark. Cool and freeze in 6 portions.
recipes.tip: One portion plus 400 g of any vegetable and a cup of water, simmered 15 minutes, is a curry.
recipes.serveWith: Rice or flatbread. Simmer with any vegetable, boiled eggs or chicken. You add: oil, spices.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin C intake: one serving gives about 29% of your daily vitamin C from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Onions supply quercetin and prebiotic fibre that feeds gut bacteria. Plum tomatoes bring vitamin C and lycopene; cooking them in a little oil makes the lycopene easier to absorb.

recipes.title: Romesco (Tatashe & Groundnut Sauce)
recipes.summary: Catalonia's roasted red pepper and nut sauce rebuilt on tatashe and toasted groundnuts, with a slice of bread for body and lime for the vinegar. For grilled chicken, roasted sweet potato, boiled yam or fish.
steps: Char the tatashe over a flame or in a hot dry pan 10 minutes, steam in a covered bowl, peel and seed.
Blend with groundnuts, garlic, bread, tomato paste, lime, paprika, salt and a quarter cup of water.
Stream in the oil while blending until thick and spoonable.
recipes.tip: Keeps a week in the fridge. Thin with water for a dressing.
recipes.serveWith: Grilled chicken or fish, roast vegetables, bread, boiled yam. You add: olive oil, tomato paste, bread.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin C intake: one serving gives about 69% of your daily vitamin C from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Tatashe (red bell pepper) has about twice the vitamin C of an orange by weight, plus beta-carotene. Groundnuts add plant protein, vitamin E, magnesium and niacin.

recipes.title: Creamy Mushroom Sauce
recipes.summary: Mushrooms browned hard with garlic and rosemary, finished with cooking cream or evaporated milk. No wine, no parmesan needed. For grilled chicken, mashed yam or boiled potatoes.
steps: Melt the butter on high heat, add the mushrooms and leave 2 minutes before stirring so they brown.
Add garlic and rosemary, 1 minute.
Add stock and simmer 2 minutes. Add cream and simmer 3 minutes until it coats a spoon.
Season, add lemon juice, spoon over the plate.
recipes.tip: Evaporated milk splits if boiled hard; keep it at a gentle simmer.
recipes.serveWith: Grilled chicken, steak, mashed yam or boiled potatoes. You add: butter, cream or evaporated milk, stock cube.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better potassium intake: one serving gives about 17% of your daily potassium from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Mushrooms bring B vitamins, selenium and potassium with almost no calories. Garlic adds allicin and vitamin B6.

recipes.title: Classic Creamy Coleslaw
recipes.summary: Half the mayo swapped for yoghurt, lime in place of vinegar, ordinary salt for celery salt. Shredded fine and rested so the cabbage softens.
steps: Whisk the mayo, yoghurt, mustard, sugar, lime juice and seasoning.
Toss with the cabbage and carrot.
Rest 30 minutes in the fridge before serving.
recipes.tip: Shred the cabbage across the grain, as thin as you can; thick slaw never softens.
recipes.serveWith: Side for jollof, fried rice, grilled chicken, fish or suya. You add: mayonnaise, yoghurt, mustard, sugar.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin K intake: one serving gives about 80% of your daily vitamin K from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Cabbage is rich in vitamin C and vitamin K and very low in calories. Carrot is the classic vitamin A source: one carrot covers a day's beta-carotene.

recipes.title: Purple Cabbage Lime Slaw
recipes.summary: No mayo: purple cabbage, onion and a whole cup of coriander dressed in lime, oil and cumin. Seeded ata rodo for jalapeño; grated carrot for colour.
steps: Whisk lime zest and juice with the oil, cumin and salt.
Toss with cabbage, onion, carrot, chilli and coriander.
Rest 15 minutes; it softens and turns a deeper purple.
recipes.tip: Keeps 3 days and does not go soggy, unlike creamy slaw.
recipes.serveWith: Fish tacos, grilled fish, suya or jollof. You add: oil, cumin, salt.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin C intake: one serving gives about 99% of your daily vitamin C from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Purple cabbage has even more vitamin C than white, plus anthocyanins. Coriander leaves add vitamin K and vitamin A.

recipes.title: Nigerian Party Coleslaw with Sweet Corn
recipes.summary: The owambe coleslaw: cabbage, carrot, green pepper and onion in salad cream, with fresh sweet corn cut off the cob instead of tinned peas.
steps: Boil the corn cob 5 minutes, cool, cut the kernels off.
Mix cabbage, carrot, pepper, onion and corn.
Fold in salad cream, mayo, sugar and salt. Chill 30 minutes.
recipes.tip: Dress it no more than an hour before the party; cabbage weeps if it sits overnight.
recipes.serveWith: Jollof rice, fried rice, chicken. You add: salad cream, mayonnaise, sugar.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin K intake: one serving gives about 107% of your daily vitamin K from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Cabbage is rich in vitamin C and vitamin K and very low in calories. Carrot is the classic vitamin A source: one carrot covers a day's beta-carotene.

recipes.title: Tabbouleh (Herb Salad)
recipes.summary: The Lebanese version is mostly parsley, not mostly grain. Bulgur is hard to find in Lagos so it is left out; extra cucumber gives body. Lemon, mint, spring onion and good oil.
steps: Salt the cucumber and tomato in a sieve for 10 minutes and drain.
Chop the parsley and mint very fine.
Toss everything with lemon, garlic, oil and salt. Rest 15 minutes.
recipes.tip: Dry the parsley completely before chopping or it turns to mush.
recipes.serveWith: Grilled chicken, fish, suya or flatbread. You add: olive oil, salt.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin K intake: one serving gives about 569% of your daily vitamin K from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Parsley is one of the richest vitamin K sources in the market; one serving covers several days' worth.

recipes.title: Fattoush with Agege Croutons
recipes.summary: Chopped lettuce, tomato, cucumber, onion and mint with crisp torn bread. Toasted day-old Agege stands in for pita, extra lemon zest for sumac, cucumber ribbons for radish.
steps: Toss the torn bread with a tablespoon of oil and salt; bake or pan-toast until crisp.
Whisk lemon juice and zest, garlic, honey, the rest of the oil and salt.
Toss the vegetables and mint with the dressing, add the croutons last.
recipes.tip: Add the bread at the table so it stays crunchy.
recipes.serveWith: Lunch on its own or beside grilled chicken. You add: bread, olive oil, honey.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin K intake: one serving gives about 105% of your daily vitamin K from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Romaine lettuce adds vitamin K, vitamin A and folate. Cherry tomatoes are a sweet source of vitamin C and lycopene.

recipes.title: Panzanella
recipes.summary: Tuscany's bread salad: ripe tomato wedges, cucumber, red onion and basil over toasted bread cubes that soak up the juices. Day-old baguette or Agege; lime if there is no vinegar.
steps: Toss bread cubes with a tablespoon of oil and toast in the oven or a pan until golden.
Whisk the remaining oil, vinegar, garlic, mustard and salt.
Toss tomatoes, cucumber, onion and bread with the dressing. Rest 20 minutes, then add basil.
recipes.tip: This is the salad for tomatoes that are too soft for anything else.
recipes.serveWith: Lunch, or beside grilled fish. You add: bread, olive oil, vinegar, optional mozzarella.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin K intake: one serving gives about 40% of your daily vitamin K from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Plum tomatoes bring vitamin C and lycopene; cooking them in a little oil makes the lycopene easier to absorb. Cucumber is mostly water with vitamin K, for hydration and crunch.

recipes.title: Caprese Salad
recipes.summary: Sliced ripe tomato, basil, oil and salt. Mozzarella is the customer's add; sliced avocado is the dairy-free stand-in that works surprisingly well.
steps: Alternate slices of tomato and cheese on a plate.
Tuck basil leaves between.
Drizzle oil, season generously, serve at once.
recipes.tip: Room-temperature tomatoes taste twice as sweet as fridge-cold ones.
recipes.serveWith: Starter or side. You add: mozzarella or avocado, olive oil, optional balsamic.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin K intake: one serving gives about 48% of your daily vitamin K from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Plum tomatoes bring vitamin C and lycopene; cooking them in a little oil makes the lycopene easier to absorb. Basil adds vitamin K and aroma.

recipes.title: Smashed Cucumber Salad
recipes.summary: Cucumbers whacked with a rolling pin so the dressing gets into the cracks: ginger, garlic, soy, a little sugar and a sliced long red chilli. Lime for rice vinegar.
steps: Smash the cucumbers with a rolling pin until they crack, then cut into chunks.
Salt them 10 minutes and drain the water.
Toss with ginger, lime, soy, sesame oil, sugar, chilli, spring onion and coriander.
recipes.tip: Serve within the hour; it is best cold and crunchy.
recipes.serveWith: Fried rice, stir-fries, grilled fish. You add: soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin K intake: one serving gives about 54% of your daily vitamin K from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Cucumber is mostly water with vitamin K, for hydration and crunch. Ginger is traditionally used for digestion and nausea.

recipes.title: Sunomono (Japanese Cucumber Salad)
recipes.summary: Paper-thin cucumber in a sweet-sour dressing. Lime plus a little sugar when there is no rice vinegar; thin strips of tatashe for colour instead of seaweed.
steps: Salt the cucumber slices 10 minutes, then squeeze out the water.
Mix vinegar, sugar, soy and a pinch of salt.
Toss with the cucumber and pepper. Chill.
recipes.tip: Squeezing the cucumber is the step people skip and then wonder why it is watery.
recipes.serveWith: Rice bowls, grilled fish, fried rice. You add: vinegar or lime, sugar, soy.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin K intake: one serving gives about 17% of your daily vitamin K from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Cucumber is mostly water with vitamin K, for hydration and crunch. Tatashe (red bell pepper) has about twice the vitamin C of an orange by weight, plus beta-carotene.

recipes.title: Kachumber (Indian Chopped Salad)
recipes.summary: Everything chopped small: cucumber, tomato, carrot, onion, cabbage, coriander, chilli, lemon. Cumin in place of chaat masala. The side that goes with any rice dish.
steps: Chop all the vegetables to the same small size.
Toss with lemon, cumin, salt and pepper.
Finish with mint.
recipes.tip: Make it just before eating; it should crunch.
recipes.serveWith: Rice, curry, jollof, grilled meat. You add: salt, cumin.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin C intake: one serving gives about 39% of your daily vitamin C from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Cucumber is mostly water with vitamin K, for hydration and crunch. Plum tomatoes bring vitamin C and lycopene; cooking them in a little oil makes the lycopene easier to absorb.

recipes.title: Shepherd's Salad (Çoban Salatası)
recipes.summary: Turkey's everyday salad: tomato, cucumber, spring onion and parsley in lemon and oil. Extra lemon zest in place of sumac; a little green pepper and mint added.
steps: Combine the vegetables and herbs.
Dress with lemon, zest, oil, salt and pepper.
Serve straight away.
recipes.tip: Chop coarse, not fine; this is a chunky salad, unlike ezme.
recipes.serveWith: Grilled meat, suya, rice. You add: olive oil, salt.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin K intake: one serving gives about 210% of your daily vitamin K from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Plum tomatoes bring vitamin C and lycopene; cooking them in a little oil makes the lycopene easier to absorb. Cucumber is mostly water with vitamin K, for hydration and crunch.

recipes.title: Melon, Cucumber & Mint Salad
recipes.summary: Sweet melon (cantaloupe) cubes with cucumber, red onion, mint and lime, a hydrating plate for the heat. Add wara or feta if you want it savoury.
steps: Whisk lime juice, oil and salt.
Toss with melon, cucumber, onion and chilli.
Add mint at the last moment.
recipes.tip: Swap in watermelon or pineapple for the melon when that is what is in season.
recipes.serveWith: Snack, side for grilled chicken, or a light lunch. You add: olive oil, optional wara.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin C intake: one serving gives about 92% of your daily vitamin C from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Sweet melon is a hydration fruit with beta-carotene and vitamin C. Cucumber is mostly water with vitamin K, for hydration and crunch.

recipes.title: Garlic Sautéed Greens (Spinach or Ugu)
recipes.summary: Three minutes, one pan. Baby spinach, ugu, efo tete or waterleaf wilted in garlic oil and finished with lime. The fastest way to put greens on a plate of rice and chicken.
steps: Warm the oil and garlic 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the leaves and toss 2 to 3 minutes until just wilted (tougher ugu takes a minute more).
Season, squeeze lime, serve.
recipes.tip: Do not cover and do not overcook; bright green means the vitamins are still there.
recipes.serveWith: Any plate: rice and stew, grilled fish, eggs. You add: oil, salt.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin K intake: one serving gives about 483% of your daily vitamin K from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Spinach is one of the richest sources of vitamin K and folate, with iron and magnesium. Garlic adds allicin and vitamin B6.

recipes.title: Charred Broccoli with Lemon & Garlic
recipes.summary: Broccoli roasted hot until the edges char, with garlic in the last minutes, lemon and a crumble of groundnuts. No oven: a very hot dry pan with a lid does the same job.
steps: Heat the oven to 220C (or a heavy pan on high). Toss broccoli with oil, salt and pepper.
Roast 15 minutes until the edges blacken; add the garlic for the last 4 minutes.
Squeeze lemon over, scatter groundnuts and chilli.
recipes.tip: Dry the florets well after washing; wet broccoli steams instead of charring.
recipes.serveWith: Grilled chicken, fish, pasta or rice. You add: oil, salt.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin K intake: one serving gives about 119% of your daily vitamin K from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Broccoli is dense in vitamin C, vitamin K, folate and fibre. Lemon juice adds vitamin C and helps the body absorb plant iron from greens.

recipes.title: Honey-Roasted Carrots with Ginger
recipes.summary: Carrot barrels roasted with a little honey and oil until caramelised, with grated ginger in the glaze and parsley on top.
steps: Toss the carrots with oil, honey, ginger, salt and pepper.
Roast at 220C for 20 minutes, turning once, until tender and browned at the edges.
Scatter parsley.
recipes.tip: Cut thicker pieces in half lengthways so everything cooks at the same rate.
recipes.serveWith: Roast or grilled chicken, rice. You add: oil, honey, salt.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin A intake: one serving gives about 118% of your daily vitamin A from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: One serving gives well over a day's vitamin A as beta-carotene, and roasting in oil makes it easier to absorb.

recipes.title: Green Beans with Groundnuts & Chilli
recipes.summary: Blistered green beans tossed with garlic, ginger, a long red chilli, spring onion and crushed roasted groundnuts. A mashed ata rodo with a splash of soy replaces chilli-garlic sauce.
steps: Heat half the oil very hot and fry the beans 5 minutes until blistered. Remove.
Add the rest of the oil, garlic, ginger and chilli, 30 seconds.
Return the beans with soy, sugar, spring onion and groundnuts. Toss 1 minute.
recipes.tip: Cook the beans in two batches if the pan is small; crowding makes them steam.
recipes.serveWith: Rice, fried rice, grilled chicken. You add: oil, soy sauce, sugar.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin K intake: one serving gives about 97% of your daily vitamin K from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Green beans bring fibre, vitamin K and folate. Groundnuts add plant protein, vitamin E, magnesium and niacin.

recipes.title: Grilled Zucchini with Lemon & Herbs
recipes.summary: Zucchini planks on a hot griddle or suya grill, then lemon, garlic, parsley and basil. A spoon of yoghurt and mint turns it into a meze.
steps: Brush the planks with oil, salt and pepper.
Grill or griddle on high 2 to 3 minutes a side until marked and tender.
Toss with garlic, herbs and a squeeze of lemon.
recipes.tip: Cut lengthways, not in rounds; planks do not fall through the grill.
recipes.serveWith: Grilled fish, chicken, suya, couscous or rice. You add: olive oil, salt.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin K intake: one serving gives about 33% of your daily vitamin K from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Zucchini is light, hydrating and adds vitamin C and potassium. Lemon juice adds vitamin C and helps the body absorb plant iron from greens.

recipes.title: Turmeric Roasted Cauliflower
recipes.summary: Cauliflower florets roasted golden with fresh grated turmeric and ginger, lemon slices in the tray, coriander to finish. Dry pepper for chilli powder.
steps: Toss florets with oil, turmeric, ginger, dry pepper, salt and pepper.
Spread on a tray with the lemon slices. Roast at 200C for 30 to 35 minutes, turning once.
Scatter coriander.
recipes.tip: Fresh turmeric is gentler than ground; two thumbs is right.
recipes.serveWith: Rice, curry, grilled chicken. You add: oil, salt.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin C intake: one serving gives about 99% of your daily vitamin C from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Cauliflower is a vitamin C and folate source with a fraction of the carbs of rice. Fresh turmeric adds curcumin; black pepper and oil improve its absorption.

recipes.title: Sautéed Mushrooms with Garlic & Parsley
recipes.summary: Mushrooms browned in an uncrowded pan, then garlic, a splash of soy, lime and parsley. Rosemary deepens it.
steps: Heat the oil until very hot. Add the mushrooms in one layer and leave 3 minutes.
Toss and cook 4 minutes more until browned.
Off the heat add garlic, soy, lime, rosemary and parsley.
recipes.tip: Salt at the end only.
recipes.serveWith: Grilled chicken, steak, rice, toast. You add: oil, soy sauce.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better potassium intake: one serving gives about 25% of your daily potassium from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Mushrooms bring B vitamins, selenium and potassium with almost no calories. Garlic adds allicin and vitamin B6.

recipes.title: Bhindi Masala (Stir-Fried Okra)
recipes.summary: Okra fried dry first so it never goes slimy, then tossed through an onion-tomato masala. Curry powder plus cumin for garam masala, fresh ginger and garlic blended.
steps: Fry the okra in 2 tablespoons of oil on medium-high 8 minutes until no longer sticky. Remove.
In the rest of the oil fry cumin seeds, then onion 5 minutes. Add blended ginger-garlic and chilli, 1 minute.
Add tomato, curry powder, turmeric and salt; cook 5 minutes.
Return the okra, toss 3 minutes, finish with coriander.
recipes.tip: Wash okra the night before and dry it completely; wet okra is slimy okra.
recipes.serveWith: Rice or flatbread. You add: oil, spices.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin K intake: one serving gives about 52% of your daily vitamin K from the produce alone.
recipes.alsoStrongIn: Vitamin C (52%), Folate (37%), Potassium (26%), Vitamin B6 (26%)
recipes.healthNote: Okra brings soluble fibre, vitamin K, folate and magnesium. Onions supply quercetin and prebiotic fibre that feeds gut bacteria.

recipes.title: Roasted Pumpkin with Lemon Yoghurt
recipes.summary: Pumpkin cubes roasted until caramelised, over a garlicky lemon yoghurt, with toasted groundnuts and coriander. Paprika for sumac.
steps: Toss pumpkin with 2 tablespoons oil, a clove of garlic, salt and pepper. Roast at 220C for 25 to 30 minutes until browned.
Mix yoghurt with the rest of the garlic, lemon, a tablespoon of oil and salt.
Spread the yoghurt on a plate, pile the pumpkin on, scatter groundnuts, coriander and paprika.
recipes.tip: Sweet potato works the same way when pumpkin is not around.
recipes.serveWith: Grilled chicken or as a light lunch with flatbread. You add: yoghurt, oil, paprika.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin A intake: one serving gives about 134% of your daily vitamin A from the produce alone.
recipes.alsoStrongIn: Vitamin C (32%), Folate (30%), Potassium (46%), Vitamin E (28%)
recipes.healthNote: Pumpkin is a beta-carotene (vitamin A) source with potassium and fibre. Lemon juice adds vitamin C and helps the body absorb plant iron from greens.

recipes.title: Crispy Smashed Potatoes with Rosemary
recipes.summary: Small Irish potatoes boiled, flattened and roasted until the edges shatter, with grated garlic and rosemary. A yoghurt-lime-coriander dip on the side.
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water 20 minutes until tender. Drain and steam dry.
Put on an oiled tray and press each one flat with a glass.
Brush with oil, garlic, salt and pepper. Roast at 220C for 25 minutes until crisp. Scatter rosemary.
recipes.tip: The flatter you smash, the crispier they get.
recipes.serveWith: Grilled chicken, fish, eggs. You add: oil, salt.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin C intake: one serving gives about 56% of your daily vitamin C from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Potatoes bring potassium, vitamin C and vitamin B6. Garlic adds allicin and vitamin B6.

recipes.title: Garlic Stir-Fried Cabbage & Carrot
recipes.summary: Thin-sliced cabbage and grated carrot in garlic oil with ginger, spring onion and a sliced chilli, finished with lime. It tastes like the vegetables in Nigerian fried rice, on their own.
steps: Heat the oil, add garlic and ginger 30 seconds.
Add cabbage, carrot and chilli. Stir-fry on high 6 to 8 minutes until softened with some browned edges.
Season, add spring onion and lime.
recipes.tip: Keep the heat high; slow-cooked cabbage smells like a school kitchen.
recipes.serveWith: Rice, stew, grilled fish, or folded into fried rice. You add: oil, salt.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin K intake: one serving gives about 135% of your daily vitamin K from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Cabbage is rich in vitamin C and vitamin K and very low in calories. Carrot is the classic vitamin A source: one carrot covers a day's beta-carotene.

recipes.title: Garlic Stir-Fried Efo Tete
recipes.summary: China cooks the same amaranth we call efo tete: a hot wok, lots of smashed garlic, oil, salt, a pinch of sugar, two minutes. Groundnut oil and a few slivers of ata rodo make it local.
steps: Wash the leaves well and shake dry.
Heat the oil very hot, add garlic and chilli 20 seconds.
Add the greens, toss constantly 2 to 3 minutes until wilted and glossy. Season with salt and sugar.
recipes.tip: Pull the leaves off the thick stems; the stems take longer and stay stringy.
recipes.serveWith: Rice, stew, grilled fish, eggs. You add: oil, salt.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin K intake: one serving gives about 1710% of your daily vitamin K from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Efo tete is high in vitamin K, vitamin A, folate and iron; quick cooking in oil keeps the vitamins and helps absorb the vitamin A.

recipes.title: Nigerian Fruit Salad with Condensed Milk
recipes.summary: The roadside classic as it should be: pineapple, pawpaw, watermelon, carrot, cucumber and coconut, with Peak milk drizzled over and roasted groundnuts on top. The milk is measured, not poured.
steps: Chop all the fruit the same size and chill.
Mix with carrot, cucumber and coconut.
Drizzle a tablespoon of condensed milk per bowl and scatter groundnuts.
recipes.tip: A tablespoon of condensed milk per person is plenty; the fruit is already sweet.
recipes.serveWith: On its own. You add: condensed milk. Groundnuts and coconut from Basket.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin C intake: one serving gives about 44% of your daily vitamin C from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Pineapple and pawpaw cover a day's vitamin C and the carrot and pawpaw add vitamin A; the groundnuts bring protein and vitamin E.

recipes.title: Filipino-Style Fruit Salad with Cream
recipes.summary: The Philippines' Christmas fruit salad, with fresh fruit instead of tinned cocktail: pineapple, pawpaw, apple, grapes, banana and fresh coconut in condensed milk and cream, chilled hard.
steps: Dice the fruit and drain off any juice.
Stir condensed milk and cream together, fold through the fruit.
Chill at least 4 hours. Add the banana just before serving.
recipes.tip: Drain the pineapple well or the cream splits.
recipes.serveWith: Party dessert. You add: condensed milk, tinned cream or thick yoghurt.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin C intake: one serving gives about 52% of your daily vitamin C from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Pineapple is rich in vitamin C and manganese, and bromelain that helps digest protein. Pawpaw is one of the richest local sources of vitamin C and beta-carotene (vitamin A), with papain for digestion.

recipes.title: Bionico (Mexican Fruit Bowl with Sweet Cream)
recipes.summary: Guadalajara's fruit cup: strawberry, sweet melon, pawpaw and pineapple under a yoghurt and condensed milk cream, topped with coconut and groundnuts in place of granola and pecans.
steps: Whisk yoghurt, condensed milk and vanilla.
Layer the fruit in glasses and spoon the cream over.
Top with coconut and groundnuts.
recipes.tip: Swap the strawberries for mango or guava when they are in season.
recipes.serveWith: Breakfast or snack. You add: yoghurt, condensed milk, vanilla.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin C intake: one serving gives about 99% of your daily vitamin C from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Strawberries deliver more vitamin C per cup than an orange, plus folate and manganese. Sweet melon is a hydration fruit with beta-carotene and vitamin C.

recipes.title: Indian Fruit Chaat
recipes.summary: Apple, banana, grapes, pawpaw and pineapple tossed with lime, mint and a salty-spicy seasoning. A pinch of yaji, salt and cumin stands in for chaat masala.
steps: Mix lime juice, yaji, cumin and salt.
Toss with the fruit and mint.
Eat within 20 minutes, before the banana browns.
recipes.tip: Salt on fruit sounds wrong until you try it.
recipes.serveWith: Snack. You add: salt, cumin, yaji.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin C intake: one serving gives about 47% of your daily vitamin C from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Apples bring soluble fibre (pectin) and polyphenols. Banana is the easy potassium and vitamin B6 source.

recipes.title: Thai Mango with Coconut Cream
recipes.summary: Mango sticky rice without the rice: ripe mango slices under a warm, lightly salted coconut cream made from a fresh Basket coconut. Add sticky rice from an Asian store if you want the full dish.
steps: Blend the coconut flesh with warm water and squeeze through a cloth for about a cup of thick coconut cream.
Warm it gently with the sugar and salt 3 minutes; do not boil.
Fan the mango slices on plates, pour the cream over, finish with lime zest.
recipes.tip: The pinch of salt is what makes it Thai; do not skip it.
recipes.serveWith: Dessert. You add: sugar, salt, optional glutinous rice.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin C intake: one serving gives about 122% of your daily vitamin C from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Mango brings vitamin A (as beta-carotene), vitamin C and folate. Fresh coconut adds fibre, manganese and satisfying fat.

recipes.title: Winter Citrus Salad with Mint & Honey
recipes.summary: Orange, grapefruit and tangerine rounds with mint, honey and pomegranate, the harmattan season plate. A squeeze of lime balances the grapefruit.
steps: Cut the peel and pith off the citrus and slice into rounds.
Arrange on a plate, scatter pomegranate and mint.
Drizzle honey and lime.
recipes.tip: Slice over a bowl and pour the collected juice back over the plate.
recipes.serveWith: Breakfast or snack. You add: honey.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin C intake: one serving gives about 87% of your daily vitamin C from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Three kinds of citrus make this the simplest way to get well over a day's vitamin C; pomegranate adds fibre and polyphenols.

recipes.title: Baked Bananas with Cinnamon & Dark Chocolate
recipes.summary: Bananas split in their skins, baked with honey and cinnamon until soft, dark chocolate melted into the slit. Works in a covered frying pan with no oven; ripe plantain gives a bigger portion.
steps: Slit each banana lengthways through the skin, not all the way through.
Drizzle honey and cinnamon into the slit. Bake at 200C for 15 minutes, or cook in a covered pan on low for 12.
Push chocolate squares into the hot slit, scatter groundnuts.
recipes.tip: Use bananas that are spotty; they bake sweeter.
recipes.serveWith: Dessert. You add: honey, cinnamon, dark chocolate.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin B6 intake: one serving gives about 35% of your daily vitamin B6 from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Banana is the easy potassium and vitamin B6 source.

recipes.title: Tropical Fruit Salad with Passion Fruit & Guava Dressing
recipes.summary: Pineapple, mango, pawpaw and kiwi dressed in passion fruit pulp and blended guava with lime. No sugar syrup; every ingredient is in the box.
steps: Blend the guava with the lime and lemon juice and strain out the seeds.
Stir the passion fruit pulp into the guava.
Pour over the diced fruit and chill 30 minutes.
recipes.tip: Make the dressing a day ahead; it keeps and gets fruitier.
recipes.serveWith: On its own. You add: nothing, or a spoon of honey if the fruit is sharp.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin C intake: one serving gives about 229% of your daily vitamin C from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Guava, kiwi, pineapple and passion fruit together give several days' worth of vitamin C in one serving, with vitamin A from the mango and pawpaw.

recipes.title: Vitamin A Plate: Mango, Pawpaw & Carrot
recipes.summary: Mango and pawpaw cubes in a lime and honey dressing, with grated carrot folded in for crunch and extra beta-carotene. Built around the three orange foods in the box.
steps: Whisk lime zest, juice and honey.
Toss with mango, pawpaw and carrot.
Chill 15 minutes and finish with mint.
recipes.tip: Orange-fleshed fruit plus a little fat (yoghurt or avocado alongside) absorbs best.
recipes.serveWith: On its own or with a spoon of yoghurt. You add: honey.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin C intake: one serving gives about 78% of your daily vitamin C from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Mango, pawpaw and carrot are all beta-carotene foods; one serving covers a day's vitamin A, with vitamin C from the lime and pawpaw on top.

recipes.title: Vitamin C Plate: Orange, Kiwi & Strawberry
recipes.summary: Orange, kiwi, strawberry and apple with lime and honey; guava added when in season because nothing beats it for vitamin C.
steps: Whisk lime juice and honey.
Toss with the fruit.
Finish with mint.
recipes.tip: Cut the apple last and toss it in the lime straight away so it stays white.
recipes.serveWith: On its own. You add: honey.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin C intake: one serving gives about 155% of your daily vitamin C from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Orange, kiwi, strawberry and guava are the four highest vitamin C fruits in the box; one serving gives more than a day's need.

recipes.title: Potassium Plate: Banana, Dates & Coconut
recipes.summary: Sliced banana, chopped dates, fresh coconut and groundnuts with a squeeze of lime: the three highest-potassium items in the box on one plate, for after training or a long day in the heat.
steps: Slice the banana and toss with lime juice.
Scatter dates, coconut and groundnuts over.
Eat at once.
recipes.tip: Freeze the banana slices first for a cold version.
recipes.serveWith: On its own or over yoghurt or oats. You add: nothing.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin B6 intake: one serving gives about 38% of your daily vitamin B6 from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Banana, dates and coconut are the potassium foods of the box; this plate gives a third of a day's potassium plus magnesium and vitamin B6.

recipes.title: Chocolate Avocado Mousse
recipes.summary: Ripe avocado blended with cocoa, fresh coconut milk and soft dates or honey into a mousse nobody can tell is avocado. Groundnuts and strawberries on top.
steps: Blend coconut flesh with half a cup of warm water and strain for coconut milk.
Blend avocado, coconut milk, dates, cocoa, vanilla and salt until completely smooth.
Chill 30 minutes. Top with strawberries and groundnuts.
recipes.tip: Taste before chilling; add a date or two if the cocoa is bitter.
recipes.serveWith: Dessert. You add: cocoa powder, honey or dates.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better folate intake: one serving gives about 54% of your daily folate from the produce alone.
recipes.alsoStrongIn: Fibre (38%), Vitamin C (27%), Vitamin K (29%), Potassium (34%)
recipes.healthNote: Avocado gives potassium, folate, vitamin E and heart-friendly fats that help absorb vitamins from the rest of the plate. Fresh coconut adds fibre, manganese and satisfying fat.

recipes.title: Fruit Skewers with Yoghurt Dip
recipes.summary: Strawberry, pineapple, banana, grapes, kiwi and mango threaded on suya sticks with a dip of yoghurt, honey and groundnut paste. Children's party food that adults finish.
steps: Whisk yoghurt, honey, groundnut paste and cinnamon.
Thread the fruit onto skewers, alternating colours.
Serve with the dip.
recipes.tip: Soak wooden suya sticks 10 minutes so the fruit slides on without splitting.
recipes.serveWith: Snack or party plate. You add: yoghurt, honey, groundnut paste.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin C intake: one serving gives about 135% of your daily vitamin C from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Strawberries deliver more vitamin C per cup than an orange, plus folate and manganese. Pineapple is rich in vitamin C and manganese, and bromelain that helps digest protein.

recipes.title: Pineapple Carpaccio with Mint & Lime
recipes.summary: Pineapple sliced so thin you can see through it, with a mint-lime oil, blueberries or pomegranate and a spoon of coconut yoghurt.
steps: Peel the pineapple and slice it paper-thin with your sharpest knife.
Bash the mint with the oil and lime zest in a pestle, or chop very fine and mix.
Lay the slices out, spoon over the mint oil, lime juice, berries and yoghurt.
recipes.tip: Chill the pineapple first; cold fruit slices thinner.
recipes.serveWith: Dessert or starter. You add: yoghurt, a little oil.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin C intake: one serving gives about 146% of your daily vitamin C from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Pineapple is rich in vitamin C and manganese, and bromelain that helps digest protein. Mint aids digestion and adds vitamin A.

recipes.title: Strawberries with Balsamic & Black Pepper
recipes.summary: Quartered strawberries macerated with a little sugar, balsamic, orange and lemon zest and black pepper. Honey and lime if there is no balsamic. Over thick yoghurt.
steps: Toss strawberries with sugar, balsamic, zests, salt and pepper.
Rest 15 to 30 minutes until syrupy.
Serve with the juices.
recipes.tip: Do not leave it longer than an hour; the berries go soft.
recipes.serveWith: Over yoghurt or on its own. You add: sugar or honey, balsamic vinegar.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin C intake: one serving gives about 72% of your daily vitamin C from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Strawberries deliver more vitamin C per cup than an orange, plus folate and manganese. One orange covers most of a day's vitamin C and adds folate and potassium.

recipes.title: Oranges with Dark Chocolate & Sea Salt
recipes.summary: Orange and tangerine rounds with a thread of olive oil, shaved dark chocolate and flaky salt. A grapefruit adds contrast; mint for colour.
steps: Slice the peeled citrus into rounds and arrange on a plate.
Drizzle the oil, scatter the chocolate and salt.
Finish with mint.
recipes.tip: Shave the chocolate with a vegetable peeler straight from the fridge.
recipes.serveWith: Dessert. You add: dark chocolate, olive oil, salt.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin C intake: one serving gives about 92% of your daily vitamin C from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Vitamin C from the citrus helps the body absorb the iron in dark chocolate.

recipes.title: Watermelon Pizza with Yoghurt & Mint
recipes.summary: A thick round of watermelon spread with honey yoghurt and topped with strawberries, kiwi, mango and mint, cut into wedges. Crushed tiger nuts and groundnuts for the granola.
steps: Cut a round slice through the middle of the watermelon and pat the surface dry.
Spread with yoghurt mixed with honey.
Top with the fruit, tiger nuts and mint. Cut into 6 wedges.
recipes.tip: Dry the watermelon surface or the yoghurt slides off.
recipes.serveWith: Snack or party plate. You add: yoghurt, honey.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin C intake: one serving gives about 45% of your daily vitamin C from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Watermelon is 92% water with potassium and lycopene: a hydration fruit. Strawberries deliver more vitamin C per cup than an orange, plus folate and manganese.

recipes.title: Honey-Baked Apples with Groundnuts & Yoghurt
recipes.summary: Apples baked with honey, cinnamon and a squeeze of lime until soft, served with yoghurt and roasted groundnuts in place of hazelnuts. Pears work the same.
steps: Core the apples and score a line around the middle so they do not burst.
Sit in a dish, drizzle honey, lime and cinnamon. Bake at 180C for 40 minutes (or covered pan, low heat, 30 minutes).
Serve warm with yoghurt and groundnuts.
recipes.tip: Spoon the pan juices back over the apples before serving.
recipes.serveWith: Dessert. You add: honey, cinnamon, yoghurt.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better fibre intake: one serving gives about 39% of your daily fibre from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Apples bring soluble fibre (pectin) and polyphenols. Groundnuts add plant protein, vitamin E, magnesium and niacin.

recipes.title: Roasted Grapes with Yoghurt & Basil
recipes.summary: Grapes roasted hot until they blister and turn jammy, spooned warm over thick vanilla yoghurt with torn basil. The bread base is optional.
steps: Toss the grapes with the oil and roast at 220C for 10 to 12 minutes until they split (a hot dry pan with a lid works too).
Stir vanilla and honey into the yoghurt.
Spoon the hot grapes and juices over the yoghurt, scatter basil.
recipes.tip: Pull them out as soon as the first ones burst; a minute more and they collapse.
recipes.serveWith: Dessert. You add: thick yoghurt, vanilla, honey, optional toast.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin K intake: one serving gives about 61% of your daily vitamin K from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Grapes bring vitamin K and resveratrol. Basil adds vitamin K and aroma.

recipes.title: Chicken Shawarma Bowl
recipes.summary: The Lagos shawarma without the wrap: spiced chicken over lettuce, tomato, cucumber and red onion with a lemon-garlic dressing and a yoghurt garlic sauce. Fresh turmeric in the marinade.
steps: Marinate the chicken 15 minutes in spices, turmeric, half the garlic, half the lemon, sliced onion and 2 tablespoons oil.
Grill or pan-fry 6 minutes a side, rest, slice.
Mix yoghurt with the remaining garlic and a squeeze of lemon.
Toss lettuce, tomato, cucumber and red onion with lemon, oil and salt.
Build bowls: salad, chicken, garlic sauce, parsley.
recipes.tip: Marinate overnight if you can; the turmeric colour deepens.
recipes.serveWith: A bowl on its own, or add rice. You add: chicken thighs, spices, olive oil, yoghurt.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin K intake: one serving gives about 279% of your daily vitamin K from the produce alone.
recipes.alsoStrongIn: Vitamin C (35%), Vitamin A (89%), Folate (118%), Potassium (35%)
recipes.healthNote: Romaine lettuce adds vitamin K, vitamin A and folate. Plum tomatoes bring vitamin C and lycopene; cooking them in a little oil makes the lycopene easier to absorb.

recipes.title: Nigerian Salad Bowl
recipes.summary: The party salad as a lunch bowl: more vegetables, less dressing. Lettuce, cabbage, carrot, tomato, cucumber, fresh sweet corn and boiled potato, with eggs and baked beans from the customer and salad cream on the side.
steps: Boil the potatoes and corn; cool and cut.
Layer lettuce, cabbage, carrot, tomato, cucumber, corn, potato and avocado in bowls.
Top with eggs and beans. Serve the salad cream on the side so each bowl is dressed to taste.
recipes.tip: Dress at the table. Pre-dressed Nigerian salad is soup by the second hour.
recipes.serveWith: Lunch on its own. You add: boiled eggs, baked beans, salad cream or mayo, optional chicken.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin K intake: one serving gives about 119% of your daily vitamin K from the produce alone.
recipes.alsoStrongIn: Fibre (38%), Vitamin C (66%), Vitamin A (48%), Folate (66%), Potassium (59%), Vitamin B6 (45%)
recipes.healthNote: Romaine lettuce adds vitamin K, vitamin A and folate. Cabbage is rich in vitamin C and vitamin K and very low in calories.

recipes.title: Mediterranean Garden Egg & Chickpea Bowl
recipes.summary: Roasted garden egg and crispy chickpeas over rice with a cherry tomato, cucumber, green pepper and parsley salad and a lemon-garlic yoghurt instead of tahini. Black-eyed beans work for the chickpeas.
steps: Toss garden egg and chickpeas with 2 tablespoons oil and salt. Roast at 220C for 25 minutes, or pan-fry in batches.
Mix tomato, cucumber, pepper and parsley with half the lemon, a tablespoon of oil and salt.
Stir the rest of the lemon and the garlic into the yoghurt.
Build bowls on rice and spinach: roasted veg, salad, yoghurt.
recipes.tip: Salt the garden egg 10 minutes and pat dry before roasting; it browns better.
recipes.serveWith: You add: rice, tinned chickpeas or cooked beans, olive oil, yoghurt.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin K intake: one serving gives about 243% of your daily vitamin K from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Garden egg is high in fibre and potassium and very low in calories. Cherry tomatoes are a sweet source of vitamin C and lycopene.

recipes.title: Roasted Vegetable & Hummus Bowl
recipes.summary: Tatashe, garden egg, mushrooms, zucchini and red onion roasted together over couscous or rice with a spring-onion hummus and spinach. The hummus can be the black-eyed bean one from this library.
steps: Toss the vegetables with oil, salt and pepper. Roast at 220C for 25 to 30 minutes, turning once.
Stir spring onion and lemon into the hummus.
Build bowls: grain, spinach, roasted vegetables, a big spoon of hummus, parsley.
recipes.tip: Roast double and keep half for tomorrow's wrap.
recipes.serveWith: You add: couscous or rice, hummus (or cooked beans to blend), olive oil.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin K intake: one serving gives about 279% of your daily vitamin K from the produce alone.
recipes.alsoStrongIn: Fibre (26%), Vitamin C (96%), Vitamin A (26%), Folate (68%), Potassium (42%), Vitamin B6 (28%)
recipes.healthNote: Tatashe (red bell pepper) has about twice the vitamin C of an orange by weight, plus beta-carotene. Garden egg is high in fibre and potassium and very low in calories.

recipes.title: Mexican Street Corn & Chicken Bowl
recipes.summary: Lime-coriander chicken over rice with charred fresh sweet corn in a creamy chilli dressing, avocado, cherry tomatoes and purple cabbage. Ata rodo for jalapeño, wara for cotija.
steps: Marinate the chicken in half the coriander, garlic, half the lime, honey, half the chilli, 2 tablespoons oil and salt. Cook the rice.
Grill or pan-fry the chicken 6 minutes a side; rest and slice.
Char the corn kernels in a hot dry pan 5 minutes. Toss with mayo, a squeeze of lime and the sliced chilli.
Stir the rest of the coriander and lime into the rice.
Build bowls: rice, chicken, corn, avocado, tomato, cabbage, cheese.
recipes.tip: Char the corn in a dry pan without stirring for the first 2 minutes.
recipes.serveWith: You add: chicken thighs, rice, mayonnaise, honey, crumbly cheese.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin C intake: one serving gives about 66% of your daily vitamin C from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Sweet corn brings fibre, B vitamins and slow-release carbohydrate. Avocado gives potassium, folate, vitamin E and heart-friendly fats that help absorb vitamins from the rest of the plate.

recipes.title: Grilled Vegetable Couscous Bowl with Yoghurt
recipes.summary: Peppers, zucchini, mushrooms and red onion grilled with garlic and rosemary over couscous or rice, with yoghurt and crushed groundnuts instead of almonds.
steps: Brush the vegetables with oil, salt and pepper and grill or griddle 10 to 12 minutes, turning, with the garlic and rosemary.
Prepare the couscous with boiling water and a little oil.
Chop the grilled garlic into the yoghurt with a pinch of salt.
Serve vegetables on couscous with yoghurt and groundnuts.
recipes.tip: Thread the mushrooms on skewers so they do not fall through the grill.
recipes.serveWith: You add: couscous or rice, olive oil, plain yoghurt.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin C intake: one serving gives about 92% of your daily vitamin C from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Tatashe (red bell pepper) has about twice the vitamin C of an orange by weight, plus beta-carotene. Zucchini is light, hydrating and adds vitamin C and potassium.

recipes.title: Esquites (Mexican Street Corn Cups)
recipes.summary: Fresh corn kernels charred in a pan then tossed warm with spring onion, coriander, chilli, garlic, lime and a spoon of mayo, with wara crumbled over. Agbado in a cup.
steps: Heat the oil very hot and add the kernels in one layer. Do not stir for 2 minutes so they char; then toss 5 minutes more.
Tip into a bowl with spring onion, coriander, chilli, garlic, lime, mayo and salt.
Spoon into cups, top with cheese and dry pepper.
recipes.tip: Stand the cob in a bowl and cut downwards; the kernels fall in, not across the kitchen.
recipes.serveWith: Snack in a cup, or a side for grilled chicken. You add: oil, mayonnaise, crumbly cheese.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin K intake: one serving gives about 44% of your daily vitamin K from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Sweet corn brings fibre, B vitamins and slow-release carbohydrate. Spring onion adds vitamin K and folate.

recipes.title: Sweet Corn Fritters
recipes.summary: Fresh corn kernels, spring onion, coriander and diced tatashe in a light batter, shallow-fried crisp. Served with the pico de gallo or a yoghurt-lime dip.
steps: Whisk flour, cornflour, baking powder, salt, egg and milk into a thick batter.
Stir in corn, spring onion, coriander and pepper.
Shallow-fry heaped tablespoons in hot oil 2 to 3 minutes a side until golden. Drain on paper.
recipes.tip: Keep the batter thick; it should barely hold the corn together.
recipes.serveWith: Snack or breakfast with a fried egg. You add: flour, cornflour, egg, milk, oil, optional cheese.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin K intake: one serving gives about 61% of your daily vitamin K from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Sweet corn brings fibre, B vitamins and slow-release carbohydrate. Spring onion adds vitamin K and folate.

recipes.title: Oven-Baked Yam Chips with Salsa
recipes.summary: A lighter dundun: yam batons tossed in garlic oil and baked crisp, dusted with yaji, with a quick tomato salsa for dipping.
steps: Soak the yam batons in cold water 10 minutes, drain and dry.
Toss with the garlic oil and salt. Bake at 220C for 20 to 25 minutes, turning once, until golden.
Mix tomato, onion, chilli, coriander, lime and a pinch of salt.
Dust the chips with yaji and serve with the salsa.
recipes.tip: Dry the yam completely before oiling; wet yam steams and goes soft.
recipes.serveWith: Snack. You add: oil, salt, yaji.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better potassium intake: one serving gives about 72% of your daily potassium from the produce alone.
recipes.alsoStrongIn: Fibre (31%), Vitamin C (57%), Vitamin K (28%), Folate (25%), Vitamin B6 (41%)
recipes.healthNote: Yam brings potassium, vitamin C and resistant starch. Plum tomatoes bring vitamin C and lycopene; cooking them in a little oil makes the lycopene easier to absorb.

recipes.title: Crispy Kale Chips
recipes.summary: Torn kale leaves massaged with a little oil and salt and baked until they shatter. Works with ugu if the leaves are dried very well. Yaji on top.
steps: Wash and dry the leaves completely.
Massage with oil and salt so every leaf is lightly coated.
Spread in one layer and bake at 150C for 20 minutes until crisp but still green.
recipes.tip: Low oven, single layer, bone-dry leaves. Any one missing gives you chewy kale.
recipes.serveWith: Snack. You add: oil, salt, yaji.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin K intake: one serving gives about 260% of your daily vitamin K from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Kale is the top green for vitamin K and also brings vitamin A and C; a handful of chips is a serving of greens.

recipes.title: Grilled Vegetable Skewers
recipes.summary: Zucchini, mushrooms, cherry tomatoes, tatashe, onion and broccoli on suya sticks, in a garlic, parsley and lemon marinade, grilled over charcoal or a griddle.
steps: Whisk oil, lemon, garlic, parsley, chilli, oregano and salt.
Thread the vegetables onto soaked skewers and brush with the marinade.
Grill on high 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until charred. Brush with more marinade to serve.
recipes.tip: Keep each skewer to one or two vegetables so everything cooks at the same speed.
recipes.serveWith: Snack, or a side for suya and grilled chicken. You add: olive oil, oregano.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin K intake: one serving gives about 136% of your daily vitamin K from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Zucchini is light, hydrating and adds vitamin C and potassium. Mushrooms bring B vitamins, selenium and potassium with almost no calories.

recipes.title: Stuffed Mushrooms with Spinach & Garlic
recipes.summary: Large mushrooms filled with shallot, garlic, chopped spinach, spring onion and breadcrumbs, baked with a little cheese. The bacon is dropped; minced beef is the customer's option.
steps: Fry the chopped stems, shallot and garlic in the oil 3 minutes. Add spinach until wilted.
Mix with breadcrumbs, spring onion, half the cheese and seasoning.
Fill the mushroom caps, top with the rest of the cheese and bake at 200C for 20 minutes.
recipes.tip: Choose caps that sit flat so the filling stays in.
recipes.serveWith: Starter or snack. You add: breadcrumbs, cheese, oil, optional minced beef.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin K intake: one serving gives about 117% of your daily vitamin K from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Mushrooms bring B vitamins, selenium and potassium with almost no calories. Spinach is one of the richest sources of vitamin K and folate, with iron and magnesium.

recipes.title: Chilli-Lime Roasted Groundnuts
recipes.summary: Raw groundnuts tossed in lime juice and zest, salt, sugar and ground dried chilli, then roasted until dry and crunchy. Yaji is the natural finishing dust.
steps: Mix lime juice, zest, chilli, salt and sugar. Toss with the groundnuts.
Spread on a tray and roast at 150C for 30 minutes, stirring every 10, until dry and crunchy.
Cool completely before storing in a jar.
recipes.tip: They crisp up as they cool; do not judge them hot from the oven.
recipes.serveWith: Snack. You add: salt, sugar, chilli powder or yaji.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better folate intake: one serving gives about 44% of your daily folate from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Groundnuts add plant protein, vitamin E, magnesium and niacin. Lime juice adds vitamin C and helps the body absorb plant iron from greens.

recipes.title: Carrot & Cucumber Yaji Sticks
recipes.summary: Carrot and cucumber batons, a wedge of lime and a pinch of yaji in a cup. The simplest snack in the library and the one people already buy at the roadside.
steps: Cut the carrot and cucumber into finger-length batons.
Stand them in a cup with the lime wedges.
Squeeze lime and dust with yaji and salt to eat.
recipes.tip: Keep the batons in cold water in the fridge; they stay crisp for two days.
recipes.serveWith: Snack. You add: yaji, salt.
recipes.healthTagline: Best for better vitamin A intake: one serving gives about 65% of your daily vitamin A from the produce alone.
recipes.healthNote: Carrot is the classic vitamin A source: one carrot covers a day's beta-carotene. Cucumber is mostly water with vitamin K, for hydration and crunch.
